description.narrative:
Afrikas kontinentala frihandelsavtal (AfCFTA) är ett av Afrikanska unionens flaggskeppsprojekt inom Agenda 2063. Huvudmålet är att ”skapa en inre marknad för varor och tjänster med fri rörlighet för människor och investeringar ”, för att öka den intra-Afrikanska handeln, stärka konkurrenskraften och stödja den ekonomiska omstruktureringen.
Att till fullo genomföra AfCFTA kommer att innebära mer än att bara implementera åtaganden i avtalet på kontinental-, regional-. och landnivå. Erfarenheterna hittills visar att genomförandet av regionala handelsavtal inom de regionala ekonomiska gemenskaperna (REC) i Afrika är ojämnt och relativt svagt. Detta beror främst på en rad marknadshinder, byråkrati, brist på infrastruktur, politiska och institutionella utmaningar, samt brist på politisk vilja att genomföra regionala åtaganden. EU AfCFTA Technical Assistance Facility (TAF) är ett Team Europe-initiativ och kommer att genomföras genom en programhanteringsenhet, bestående av GIZ, Expertise France och eventuellt FIAAP (Spanien). Bidrag till TAF kommer från Europeiska Kommissionen, BMZ (Tyskland), AFD (Frankrike) och Sverige. Sida kommer att bidra via ett överföringsavtal med Europeiska kommissionen.
Programmet består av två komponenter, ett institutionellt stöd och ett efterfrågestyrt instrument där enskilda länder, regionala organisationer främst kan söka stöd i form av: studier, utbildning, teknisk expertis m.m.

The African Continental Free Trade Agreement (AfCFTA) is one of the African Union's flagship projects in Agenda 2063. The main objective is to "create a single market for goods and services with free movement of people and investment", to increase intra-African trade, strengthen competitiveness and support economic restructuring. Fully implementing the AfCFTA will involve more than just complying with state, regional and continental requirements and obligations in the agreement. Experience to date shows that the implementation of regional trade agreements within the Regional Economic Communities (RECs) in Africa is uneven and relatively weak. This is mainly due to a number of market barriers, bureaucracy, lack of infrastructure, political and institutional challenges, and a lack of political will to implement regional commitments. The EU AfCFTA Technical Assistance Facility (TAF) is a Team Europe initiative and will be implemented through a programme management unit, consisting of GIZ, Expertise France and possibly FIAAP (Spain). Contributions to the TAF will come from the European Commission, BMZ (Germany), AFD (France) and Sweden. Sida will contribute through a transfer agreement with the European Commission. The programme consists of two components, an institutional support and a demand-driven instrument where individual countries, regional organizations can primarily apply for support in the form of: studies, education, technical expertise, etc.

The AfCFTA is one of the AU flagship projects under the ten-year implementation plan of its Agenda 2063. The main objective is to create a free trade area for goods and services, as well as enhance competitiveness, and support economic transformation and industrialization in Africa.
Due to the low level of intra-regional trade in Africa and the high costs related to trading across borders in the African continent, supporting further trade integration and harmonization is a priority for the AU and its member states to promote economic diversification and industrialization that leads to economic development, employment and poverty reduction.
Through an EU regional "Team Europe Initiative" (TEI), within the current EU regional multiannual indicative program 2021-2027, the EU Technical Assistance Facility (EU-TAF) to the AfCFTA was created by the EU and participating member states. The EU-TAF is currently jointly financed by the EU Commission, France, Germany, Sweden, Denmark, Netherlands and Ireland. The facility is meant to be an efficient, reactive and flexible mechanism to answer to the needs of the African Union (AfCFTA Secretariat, AUC and some AU specialized agencies), RECs, its Member States and potentially regional private sector organizations relevant to the AfCFTA.
The overall objective of the EU-TAF is to contribute to the African economic integration process through the realization of the African Continental Free Trade Area.
The specific objectives of the Action are to contribute to enhancing the capacity for preparing and conducting the remaining negotiations (all phases) of the AfCFTA. Strengthening the institutional capacity of targeted African institutions and countries to successfully implement the AfCFTA priority areas and manage the next steps towards a single market.

title.narrative: Transfer agreement OUA.PANAF.2021.41853.SE TAF to support the ACFTA negotiation and implementation

description.narrative:
The EU-TAF implemented a wide variety of activities to strengthen the organisational and institutional capacity of the AfCFTA Secretariat in Accra. The support focussed on the thematic areas of Market Access, Rules of Origin, and NonTariff Measures (NTM) with the Directorate for Trade in Goods and Competition. In the area of customs cooperation and trade facilitation, the programme supported the development of several important strategies. These include the continental Trade Facilitation Strategy, the Strategy for Facilitation of Fastlane Clearance of Urgent and Relief Goods such as food and pharmaceuticals, and an Awareness Raising Strategy for trade facilitation through regional awareness campaigns.
Technical and logistics support was provided to both Directorates of the AU Economic Development, Trade, Tourism, Industry and Minerals Department (ETTIM). The support to ETTIM revolved around two workstreams: 1) Support to the revision of the African MultiDimensional Regional Integration Index (AMRII) and the development of a new index called the African Synthetic Regional Integration Index (ASRII) and, 2) Development of a Strategy on Diversifying and Growing Africas Exports.
The support also included the implementation of key industrialization and trade policy frameworks and initiatives such as the Accelerated Industrial Development of Africa (AIDA), the AU SME Strategy, the Africa Union Commodity Strategy, the African Mining Vision (AMV), the African Tourism Strategic Framework, as well as the operationalization of the Enterprise African Network.
In alignment with the work programme, the EU-TAF implemented activities with six RECs that had requested technical assistance under the Call for Proposals published in the autumn of 2023. The partners for these interventions included the EAC Secretariat, the IGAD Secretariat, the SADC Secretariat, the COMESA Secretariat, the ECCAS Commission, and the ECOWAS Commission. The work covered a range of thematic areas, with a focus on institutional strengthening and strategy development on various subtopics within trade in goods.
Furthermore, the support to the Member States continued throughout 2024. The activities differed between the Member States, but focused largely on institutional strengthening of public sector entities responsible for coordinating the national AfCFTA agenda, and on support to the private sector covering both capacity building on the provisions of the AfCFTA and export promotion.
Lastly, collaboration with continental and regional private sector organizations were strengthened further in 2024. Following extensive consultations at the start of 2024, the programme commenced implementation of activities with the Pan African Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PACCI) as the only continental private sector organisation, as well as with the East African Business Council (EABC), the COMESA Business Council (CBC), and the Regional Consular Chamber of UEMOA (RCCUEMOA) as regional private sector organisations, ensuring wide regional coverage. The support focussed on strengthening the organisational capacities of several national Chambers of Commerce, including on the AfCFTA provisions.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
